poses.name: Seated neutral at halt, sword upright at the right shoulder
poses.description: Seat and legs first: pelvis centred and upright (tilt 3), thighs 50 below horizontal, knees bent 70, heels down. Then trunk straight, ear over shoulder over hip over heel. Right fist holds the sword upright with the hilt at the shoulder; left fist holds both reins low behind the withers, little finger between them; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left.
poses.ref_notes: seat-neutral-1: halted rider with the sword upright and a large round shield (Carnuntum). -3: distant halted riders for the sitting posture. Converted from the earlier table by hand; no still shows the sword exactly at the shoulder.

sources.credit: Codrin.B (uploader of the series; verified on the -021 page) via Wikimedia Commons

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Seated at ease, sword resting point down on the right thigh
poses.description: Relaxed halt. Pelvis settled back (tilt -5), back slightly rounded, legs hanging looser. The sword hangs from an almost straight right arm beside the right thigh, blade forward and down past the knee (a fist round a handle cannot bring a blade into line with the arm, so it does not hang straight down). Left fist holds the reins low and loose; shield lies over the left thigh.
poses.ref_notes: seat-at-ease-1 and -2: riders sitting relaxed at a halt; the point-down sword is from general practice, no still shows it.
poses.description_v2: Relaxed halt. Pelvis settled back (tilt -5), back slightly rounded, legs hanging looser. The sword hangs from an almost straight right arm, point down against the right thigh. Left fist holds the reins low and loose; shield lies on the left thigh.

rein_arm.from_the_text: reins low and loose; shield lies over the left thigh

poses.name: Seated walk, sword at the shoulder
poses.description: Seat follows the horse's back; pelvis rolls forward a few degrees each stride, shoulders level. Sword rests upright in the hollow of the right shoulder; reins in the left fist in light contact.
poses.ref_notes: walk-seat-1 and -2: medieval reenactment riders at a walk from the side and rear; seat and rein hand taken, weapons are lances.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Rising trot, up
poses.description: Pelvis lifted just clear of the saddle by the knees, trunk inclined a little forward, hips and knees closed. The seat support is nominal for this instant. Sword carried at the shoulder, left fist steady.
poses.ref_notes: trot-seat-dressage: dressage trot, side view; trunk inclination taken. The rise itself is not shown; built from the half-seat notes.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Rising trot, down
poses.description: Back in the saddle: pelvis down and slightly tilted, trunk nearly upright. Same arms as the up phase.
poses.ref_notes: trot-seat-dressage: a dressage rider seated in trot, trunk nearly upright; used for the down phase only.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Canter seat
poses.description: Deep seat with the pelvis rocking forward and back through the three-beat stride; trunk upright, small inward twist of the chest. Sword at the shoulder, reins low.
poses.ref_notes: No canter still of a sword-carrying rider was kept; built from the walk seat and the seated canter description in the seat note.

sources.credit: Codrin.B (uploader of the series; verified on the -021 page) via Wikimedia Commons

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Gallop, forward (two-point) seat
poses.description: Seat out of the saddle and over the heels: pelvis pitched forward 18, trunk folded 14 more, knees closed to 90, heels down. Head up to look ahead. Sword carried forward and up in a bent arm; left fist forward over the withers.
poses.ref_notes: gallop-forward-seat-1 and -2: jockey and cavalry riders in the forward seat; torso and knee angles by eye.

sources.credit: Eadweard Muybridge and University of Pennsylvania (Wellcome Library, London) via Wikimedia Commons

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist forward over the withers

poses.name: Halt and rein-back, leaning back
poses.description: Pelvis tilts back (-8) and the trunk leans a few degrees behind the vertical, heels pushed down, left fist raised and drawn back toward the belly to ask the horse to stop or step back.
poses.ref_notes: rein-check-1 and -2: riders sitting back with the hand drawn in; lean amount judged by eye.

sources.credit: Unknown author (1932 book by Yusa Kohei; public domain, Japan, published before 1958) via Wikimedia Commons
Unknown author (E. Beudant, Exterieur et Haute Ecole, 1923; public domain, anonymous pre-1931) via Wikimedia Commons

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist raised and drawn back toward the belly

poses.name: Turn in the saddle, left
poses.description: Pelvis follows the horse's left turn (+5), chest twists 20 left and head looks 60 left into the turn. Left fist moves left over the neck; shield swings forward.
poses.ref_notes: turn-left-1 and -2: riders looking into a left turn; chest and head twist by eye.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist moves left over the neck; shield swings forward

poses.name: Turn in the saddle, right
poses.description: Mirror of the left turn with a bearing rein: pelvis -5, chest twists 20 right, head 60 right; the left fist crosses to the right over the withers; shield stays near the left thigh.
poses.ref_notes: Mirror variant of the left-turn references; not photographed.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist crosses to the right over the withers

poses.name: Look behind
poses.description: Seat fixed; chest twisted 35 right and head 70 right to look back over the right shoulder. Sword and reins unchanged.
poses.ref_notes: look-behind-1 and -2: riders twisted round to look back; twist split between chest and head by eye.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Cut down to the right, wind-up
poses.description: Seat and legs unchanged. Chest turns 15 right, right arm raised and cocked: upper arm turned out so the sword rests behind the right shoulder, blade leaning back. Left fist stays low.
poses.ref_notes: cut-windup-high-1 and -2: sword raised behind the shoulder on horseback; arm external rotation chosen so the forearm points up.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Cut down to the right, strike
poses.description: Seat bones stay down. Trunk bends from the waist 20 forward and 24 to the right with the chest turned 25 right; right arm extends outward and down, blade angled down and outward. Right thigh opens slightly.
poses.ref_notes: cut-down-right-1 and -2: riders striking down on the right side; lean and arm line by eye.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Cut down to the right, follow-through
poses.description: Blade swept down past the right leg and backward; trunk bent 25 forward and 25 right, chest turned 30 right, head following the blade. Left fist still low.
poses.ref_notes: cut-followthrough-right-1 and -2: end of a downward cut on horseback.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Cross-body cut to the left over the horse's neck
poses.description: Chest turned 25 left, trunk bent 8 forward; the right arm crosses the body, forearm turned over (pronated 60), the sword sweeping from the right shoulder across to the left past the horse's neck. Left fist held back and low so the reins stay slack.
poses.ref_notes: cut-left-across-1 and -2: riders cutting across to the left; arm roll by eye.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist held back and low so the reins stay slack

poses.name: Forward point at the charge
poses.description: Trunk leaning 18 forward over the pommel, chest turned 12 left, right arm extended forward with the sword level at the front, elbow still bent 25. Shield held forward on the left forearm.
poses.ref_notes: sword-point-forward-1 and -2: riders with an arm and weapon level to the front; wrist ulnar deviation taken at the 20 limit.

rein_arm.from_the_text: shield held forward on the left forearm

poses.name: Overhead cut, at the strike
poses.description: Sword brought up and over, now falling forward: right arm elevated 105 and bent 65, trunk folded 15 forward, chin tucked. Seat down; left fist low.
poses.ref_notes: No usable photograph of a mounted overhead strike; numbers built from the wind-up reference and keeping elevation under the 120 armour limit.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Shield cover, left
poses.description: Chest turned 10 left, left arm raised and out 40 so the shield covers the rider's left side; the reins stay in the fist, which lifts with the forearm.
poses.ref_notes: shield-cover-left-1 and -2: riders with the shield raised to the left.

rein_arm.kept: left arm raised and out so the shield covers the left side: the authored arm does this

poses.name: Shield cover, front
poses.description: Trunk leans 18 forward, head ducks behind the shield; the left upper arm is raised to horizontal and the forearm stands up, holding the shield in front of face and chest.
poses.ref_notes: shield-cover-front-high-1 and -2: shield raised in front of the face.

rein_arm.from_the_text: the forearm stands up, holding the shield in front of face and chest

poses.name: Brace for impact
poses.description: Pelvis forward 10 and trunk bent 20 more, head tucked behind the shield; legs clamp tight (knees 80). Shield raised in front on the left; the sword held upright against the right side, elbow bent about 120.
poses.ref_notes: shield-cover-front-high-1 for the raised shield. The crouch, tuck and sword position have no reference.

rein_arm.from_the_text: shield raised in front on the left

poses.name: Hit reaction in the saddle
poses.description: Struck on the right: pelvis tilts back, trunk folds 18 forward and twists 22 left, bent 12 left; head snaps away. Right arm flung out, the sword swinging down and out; left fist jerks up, shield slides forward.
poses.ref_notes: No reference; built from the spine limits and kept inside the armour limits (twist 35, side bend 25).

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist jerks up, shield slides forward

poses.name: Victory, sword raised
poses.description: Seat firm, chest lifted and slightly arched, head up. Right arm raised high, fist above the head, the sword pointing up and forward; left fist keeps the reins at the belly.
poses.ref_notes: seat-neutral-1 for the upright seat and sword; the overhead arm is built from the limits (118 is under the 120 armour limit).
poses.description_v2: Seat firm, chest lifted and slightly arched, head up. Right arm raised to 118 with the sword upright overhead; left fist keeps the reins at the belly.

rein_arm.from_the_text: left fist holds both reins low behind the withers; the shield hangs on the left forearm, face to the left

poses.name: Balance while the horse rears
poses.description: The horse's back is tilted about 45 up, so the rider folds forward to stay over the feet: pelvis 25 and trunk 25 more forward, knees closed to 100, heels down. Left fist forward and low on the neck with the shield on the forearm; right arm out with the sword up for balance.
poses.ref_notes: rear-balance-by-horse: rider leaning forward and gripping while the horse rears. rear-rider-2009-115: rider holding a lance upright through a rear. Trunk lean read by eye from both.

sources.credit: Mona Hassan Abo-Abda via Wikimedia Commons

rein_arm.kept: left fist forward and low on the neck: the authored arm does this

seat_width: Version 2 (2026-10-09): every thigh is spread 20 degrees further than in version 1 (20 to 40; the pose library's limit of 45 caps the two widest). The T1 Paladin horse at withers 0.50 asks about 37 to 41 degrees of spread from this rider (output/t1-paladin-claude/v4/horse/work/tack.json, rider_on_horse.hip_spread_estimate); version 1 was written before the horse existed. Provisional until the mounted fit aims the seat on the bound horse. Version 1 is kept in output/t1-paladin-claude/v4/poses-paladin-v1.json.
items_placed: Version 3 (2026-10-09), for the T1 Paladin Default rider as bound (output/t1-paladin-claude/v4/work/bound-b2.npz). Legs and seat are version 2's. Left arms: written from the rein fist's place and the shield's facing by output/t1-paladin-claude/v4/scripts/p4_author_reins.py (each pose's `rein_arm` record); each shield entry is where that arm puts the shield. Right arms: solved by hb_item_aim.py --fix --place --clear from a place for the sword's grip (statures from the pelvis, root axes) and the blade's direction, written from each pose's own description; two blades restated to what a fist round a handle can do (seat-at-ease, victory-sword-raised; their earlier texts are kept as description_v2). Version 2 is kept in output/t1-paladin-claude/v4/poses/paladin-v2.json. Provisional until the mounted fit checks every hand and blade against the horse.
rein_arms: Left arms written by output/t1-paladin-claude/v4/scripts/p4_author_reins.py from the rein fist's place and the shield's facing (each pose's `rein_arm` record); each shield entry is where that arm puts the shield.
wrist_eased: Sword arms with the forearm rolled more than 45 degrees solved again by output/t1-paladin-claude/v4/scripts/p4_ease_wrist.py (the baseline's hb_item_aim.place with the roll's range narrowed); each pose's `wrist_eased` record says what moved.
